user_prompt: What is the effect of single-incision mid-urethral slings (SIS; any commercial device except TVT-Secur, e.g. Ajust, Needleless/Contasure, MiniArc, Ophira, Altis, Solyx) compared with transobturator mid-urethral slings (TOT/TVT-O, inside-out or outside-in) on subjective cure or improvement of stress urinary incontinence at 12 months in women undergoing surgery for stress or stress-predominant urinary incontinence?  Effect measure: pool as a risk ratio (RR) of the proportion cured or improved, SIS divided by TOT. RR > 1 means more women cured or improved with the single-incision sling.  Outcome: number of women reporting subjective cure or improvement of incontinence (events) out of the number analysed in each arm (total), at the 12-month follow-up. - Use the patient-reported cure/improvement definition the paper gives (e.g. no stress leakage by questionnaire, "very much" or "much improved" on a global impression scale, or satisfaction-based success). Do not use objective cure (cough stress test, pad test, urodynamics). - Use the 12-month assessment. If the paper is a longer follow-up report (24 or 36 months), read the 12-month figures from its tables or figures; do not use the longest follow-up. If 12 months is not reported, use the closest earlier assessment of at least 6 months. - Be careful with arm labels. In some papers the single-incision arm is listed first, in others second. Assign arms by the device description (single-incision / mini-sling vs transobturator tape), not by column position, and keep SIS as the treatment group in every study. - Trials with more than one single-incision arm: report each eligible single-incision arm separately against the shared TOT group, and divide the TOT group's size and events equally across the comparisons so the same women are not counted twice. - Trials that also include a TVT-Secur arm: ignore the TVT-Secur arm and keep any other single-incision arm. - Multiple reports of the same trial: extract once, and prefer the report that gives the 12-month subjective result.  Do not pool objective cure, quality-of-life scores, complications, operating time, pain, reoperation or the 12-to-24-month outcome. Exclude trials that include only TVT-Secur, trials comparing a sling with colposuspension, bulking agents or retropubic slings, and trials with no TOT arm.
